sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is Human Rights Watch's March 2026 statement on India's Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, characterising it as a major setback to the 2014 NALSA self-identification right and the 2019 Act's protections.

BBC report (26 March 2026) on the amendment bill narrowing trans self-identification, passed by both houses and pending presidential assent: it limits recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, makes board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery, and sparked protests; the Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and critics (including activists Laxman Narayan Tripathi and Grace Banu) warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people.

Times of India (Kolkata, 18 August 2024): a transwoman travelling to an RG Kar Medical College protest alleges a railway-police constable groped her at Rabindra Sadan metro station as a 'gender check'; police denied it and filed a counter-FIR. Shared national source: it evidences the policing practice of treating trans appearance as a suspicion category, which recurs in checkpoints and transit spaces countrywide rather than in this unit specifically.

localsOnly: One of the 12 states/UTs that has constituted the legally mandated transgender welfare board — though an RTI investigation found most such boards rudderless, so this matters for residents' access to scheme delivery, not for visitors.
